content.text: Localized collection of pus in breast tissue
MC in lactating women 2° to nipple trauma (esp. primigravida)
breast pain (esp. one quadrant) w/ tenderness,
drainage via needle aspiration (lactational abscess) or I&D
a contraindication to breast feeding – milk drainage
is important to facilitate resolution of infection
Benign solid tumor composed of glandular & fibrous tissue
MC benign breast mass (after fibrocystic dz)
tender prior to menstruation) typically 1-2cm in diameter
nontender, rubbery, well-defined, freely mobile mass
▪︎gradually grow over time, size may wax/wane w/ cycles
fibrous tissue & collagen arranged in a “swirl”
: may be needed if enlarging after repeat U/S or for large masses
Noncancerous, fluid-filled breast cysts due to exaggerated response to hormones
*MC benign breast disorder in reproductive age
(test of choice): dense, prominent, fibroglandular tissue w/ cysts but
straw-colored or green fluid w/ no blood
: observation, supportive bra, low fat diet, reduce caffeine & chocolate intake, warm/cool compress, analgesics, evening primrose oil or vitamin E
*FNA removal or fluid is diagnostic & therapeutic in
Infection of the breast MC in lactating women
Imaging reserved for cases not responsive to empiric ABX within 48-72h
: warm/cool compresses, breast pump, anti-inflammatory medications
▪︎erythromycin can be used in PCN allergy
*continue breastfeeding – milk drainage is critical for
resolution of infection & relief of SXS
